checks.claim: Lemma 27.1: Gamma recurrence, Beta-Gamma product and duplication with half-Gamma
checks.reason: Hand-checked. The boundary term u^x e^-u vanishes for x>0. The map (u,v)=(Rt,R(1-t)) has Jacobian R. The substitutions t=(1+v)/2 and v^2=w give Beta(x,x)=4^(1-x)*(1/2)*Beta(1/2,x)=2^(1-2x)Beta(1/2,x). Gamma(1/2)=int_R e^(-z^2)dz, and its square is 2pi*int_0^inf r e^(-r^2)dr=pi. Substitution gives Gamma(2x)=2^(2x-1)Gamma(x)Gamma(x+1/2)/sqrt(pi). This matches the GI Eq5 excerpt, with symbols s,u renamed x,w.

checks.claim: Lemma 27.2: binomial series and exact incomplete-Beta factors for 0<s<1
checks.reason: The termwise ODE (1-z)y'=py holds because (p)_(n+1)-n(p)_n=p(p)_n, so (1-z)^p y is constant one. With -a=2r-1, t=su gives the prefactor s^(1+2r-1-r)=s^r. Beta(n+1-r,2r)/Beta(1-r,2r)=(1-r)_n/(1+r)_n, and (r)_n/(1+r)_n=r/(r+n). Expanding (1-u)^(r-1) in B_s reproduces L(s)=r Beta(1-r,2r)B_s(r,r). The arguments su and u<s stay below 1, and Tonelli applies to nonnegative terms.

checks.claim: Lemma 27.2: K*f_a=1 for every s in [0,1], endpoints handled separately, L1/L2, exact mass with no renormalization
checks.reason: Reflection gives the right part L(1-s), and B_s+B_(1-s)=Beta(r,r). Next, r Beta(1-r,2r)Beta(r,r)=r Gamma(1-r)Gamma(r)^2/Gamma(1+r)=Gamma(r)Gamma(1-r). The endpoint s=0 is directly Beta(r,1-r), and s=1 follows by reflection, with no limit used. L2 uses -2r=a-1>-1. M_a=Gamma(1-r)/(Gamma(2-2r)Gamma(r))=Gamma((1+a)/2)/(Gamma(1+a)Gamma((1-a)/2)). A hand evaluation at a=.5 gives about .3814 and at a=.25 about .6677, consistent with the retained diagnostic, which is not relied on as proof. No spatial theorem or rough field is imported.
